title: UK labour market overview — earnings, unemployment and vacancies (ONS, 07:00 London / 02:00 ET), the print whose Jul–Sep window IS the Bank's forecast Q3
source: EST: two publisher primaries fetched direct 2026-09-09, both HTTP 200. (1) ons.gov.uk/releases/uklabourmarketnovember2026 — the ONS release-calendar entry reads verbatim 'UK Labour Market: November 2026', 'Release date: 17 November 2026 7:00am', 'Estimates of employment, unemployment, inactivity, average weekly earnings, vacancies and other labour market related statistics for the UK', marked 'This release is not yet published.' (2) gov.uk/government/statistics/announcements/uk-labour-market-november-2026 — the UK's statutory pre-announcement register reads verbatim '17 November 2026 7:00am (confirmed)', producer Office for National Statistics. Filed estimate on this lane's no-self-confirm limit and because the confirmed-prefix taxonomy in market-events-data.ts carries BLS:/BEA:/CENSUS:/FED: and no slot for the UK Office for National Statistics — the same gap uk-labour-market-2026-09-15 and uk-labour-market-2026-10-20 were filed under. The DATE is not in doubt; the estimate label is about the taxonomy, not the evidence. Proposed 2026-09-09 by the uk-labour-market-2026-10-20 lane; researched and made canonical by its own lane the same day
notes: RESEARCHED 2026-09-09 by its own lane (docs/research/events/uk-labour-market-2026-11-17.md), which read the single proposal in full and re-fetched every primary rather than inheriting it. The proposal it supersedes — proposals/uk-labour-market-2026-11-17.from-uk-labour-market-2026-10-20.json — is now inert and stays where it is. TITLE AMENDED, and the amendment is this entry's finding. The proposal filed it as 'the first wage read AFTER the Budget and the November MPR, and the one that scores both'. The MPR half is right and the BUDGET half is wrong twice over: the AWE/LFS reference window is Jul-Sep 2026, wholly BEFORE the 2026-10-28 Budget, and UK employer-cost measures conventionally take effect the following April (Autumn Budget 2024-10-30 raised secondary Class 1 NICs from 13.8% to 15% and cut the threshold to GBP 5,000 effective April 2025 — a five-month lag), so no Budget wage response is observable in this print at all. What the print IS, exactly and arithmetically, is the Bank's forecast quarter: AWE is a three-month average, Jul-Sep 2026 IS 2026 Q3, and the July 2026 MPR projects private-sector AWE growth 'around 3.0% in Q3'. The 2026-10-20 print straddles (Jun-Aug, two-thirds Q3); this one matches with zero window mismatch, which is why its kill threshold is TIGHTER (>=3.3%) than the 10-20 lane's (>=3.4%), not looser. IMPACT LOW, argued not inherited: symbols [], this repo tracks no UK-listed symbol and no house playbook is rates- or sterling-keyed; the measured cable reaction to the 2026-08-18 release was ~0.1% on a two-sided beat. Operational note: at 07:00 London / 02:00 ET this is the first macro release of the ET session by 6.5 hours (retail-sales-2026-11-17 and import-export-prices-2026-11-17 at 08:30 ET, industrial-production-2026-11-17 at 09:15 ET, mtis-2026-11-17 and nahb-hmi-2026-11-17 at 10:00 ET) — but UNLIKE 2026-10-20 there is no FOMC blackout running, and fomc-minutes-2026-11-18 lands the next day, so the pre-dawn attribution here is weaker than the October sibling's. The November corridor also does NOT repeat October's same-minute collision: ONS publishes CPI on 2026-11-18 and public sector finances on 2026-11-20, separate mornings (both primaries fetched 2026-09-09). Estimate widens caution only; nothing date-keyed may act on this.
